pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are 0 and done=2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks / and ?view=open list only open items in id order; src/index.js uses WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id.
test 'AC-3' marks 3 and 1 done, expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] with status 200.
test 'AC-4' expects all three items in id order with only the done one marked.
test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /; the current view is <strong>, not a link.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__; the code uses Object.hasOwn.

The behaviour is implemented and tested, but the follow-up commit 8d91420 removed 'AC-7:' from the test title. No test now names AC-7, and the spec does not mark it 'verified by review'. By the rule that an item no test names is unmet, it is unmet.
traffic/routes.json contains /?view=done and /?view=all; test 'AC-8' asserts both are present.

findings.what: Commit 8d91420 ('Follow-up edits') renamed the AC-7 test to 'an empty table says so in every view...', dropping the AC-7 label. No test now names AC-7, so the item is unmet under the naming rule. The PR claims the file covers AC-1 to AC-8, which is no longer true by name.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7:' in the test title. Optionally split the test into one per message (Nothing open., Nothing done yet., No items yet. in each view).

findings.what: The PR says test/done.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8, but the AC-7 test lost its label in the last commit. The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' also hides a late commit that edited a test.
findings.fix: Restore the label and correct the PR body.

findings.what: The 'Empty table' state test only checks the default view. Other views are covered only in the combined test, which has lost its AC label.
findings.fix: Rely on the restored AC-7 test, or add the other views to the state test.

findings.what: The README does not say that an unknown view answers 400, which the PR lists as a behaviour change.
findings.fix: Add one sentence about the 400 for other view values.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions: it opens on open items and uses a query parameter. It adds no write route.
7 of 8 acceptance items are met. AC-7 lost its test label in the last commit. Every state-table row has a test.
The assertions check behaviour. I could not run npm test: vitest is not installed in this copy. The traffic fake-app test change widens the fake app and loosens nothing.
The README describes the views but not the 400 response.
Object.hasOwn guards the view lookup. The SQL is built only from fixed strings. The empty-table check runs a second query only when the result is empty.
The view value is allow-listed, titles are HTML-escaped, and no injection path was found. The traffic route regex now allows '?', but not whitespace or '#'.
The page is a minimal server-rendered HTML list with no styling or UI components. No screenshots were available.
There is no browser in this session, so I could not check the UI flow. The nav HTML is covered by string-level tests.
The title is within 72 characters. The 'covers AC-1 to AC-8' claim is false by name, and 'Changed after the go: nothing' omits the late test edit.
